verdict.rationale: iTerm2 ships an optional AI plugin and a built-in LLM chat that can run commands on your behalf. A hands-on user reports prompting it in natural language to produce an awk command, so natural-language-to-command generation exists. It requires installing a separate plugin and supplying your own API key, and no evidence shows the generated command being inserted in place at the shell prompt rather than produced in a separate chat or toolbox window. missing for 10: documented in-place insertion of the generated command at the prompt, first-party docs describing the command-generation workflow in depth, use without a separate plugin or own API key.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can type natural language and get the right shell command generated in place

citations.quote: This is an optional component you can install to enable generative AI features in iTerm2.
Link sessions to get context-aware help, run commands on your behalf, or explain output with annotations.
One user prompted the iTerm2 AI feature to use awk to filter the 2nd and 5th columns of piped input and truncate the 5th to 25 chars.
